title: Knowledge Transfer Scaling Laws for 3D Medical Imaging
claim: Different domains scale at different rates and transfer asymmetrically, following power laws and revealing a hub-and-island structure that motivates transfer-aware allocation.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: two log-log line plots, then a heatmap
description: Three side-by-side panels, each with a bold title. Panel (a) is a log-log plot of MAE validation loss against training budget T (10K to 200K). It shows six colored scatter series with fitted straight lines, one for each of six imaging domains. The legend lists a β exponent per domain, and a note says β varies 3.5× across domains. The lines in purple and blue have clearly different slopes. Panel (b) is a log-log plot of MAE loss on the target domain. It has three fitted lines: a solid dark one, a dashed blue one and a dotted purple one. The legend gives the transfer discounts τ for ABD CT→ABD MRI, ABD MRI→ABD CT and ABD CT→HN PET. Panel (c) is a 6×6 heatmap of the transfer matrix τij, with source on the x-axis and target on the y-axis. The diagonal is dark navy, off-diagonal cells are shaded from white to blue, and each cell has a number. There is a colorbar on the right. The eye goes first to the heatmap diagonal and the crossing lines.
caption: Observations motivating the transfer-aware scaling law. (a) Per-domain MAE loss follows Li = Ei + Ci/T βi with domain-specific exponents varying 3.5× (β = 0.21 for BRAIN T1 to β = 0.76 for HN PET), indicating that domains benefit from additional data at fundamentally different rates. (b) Cross-domain transfer obeys the same power-law form with a directional discount τij: ABD CT transfers strongly to ABD MRI (τ=0.56) but weakly to HN PET (τ=0.04), and the reverse ABD MRI →ABD CT (τ=0.42, dashed) is weaker than the forward direction. (c) Full 6×6 transfer matrix τij (from source j to target i) estimated from pure-domain proxy runs. The matrix is asymmetric (τij̸ = τji) and reveals hub-and-island structure: ABD CT (hub) transfers broadly to most domains, while HN PET (island) is largely isolated.
abstract: Vision foundation models are increasingly moving beyond 2D to volumetric domains such as 3D medical imaging, where unified pretraining across different imaging modalities (i.e. CT, MRI, and PET) could provide foundational models for diverse clinical tasks. However, training such models requires mixing heterogeneous imaging domains, and current mixture strategies remain largely heuristic. In this work, we observe that different medical imaging domains scale at variable rates during pretraining, and knowledge transfer between domains is strongly asymmetric: training on one domain can substantially improve another, but the reverse may be much weaker. Interestingly, both MAE reconstruction loss and cross-domain transfer follow predictable power-law trends with domain-specific behaviors. Motivated by these findings, we formulate data allocation as a scaling-law optimization problem. The derived allocations reveal an interpretable hub-and-island structure: highly transferable domains emerge as hubs that benefit many others and deserve strategic allocation, while isolated domains act as islands requiring direct investment. Empirically, transfer-aware allocation outperforms data-proportional sampling by up to 58% and generalizes well to unseen budgets with r=0.989. Downstream validation on disease classification and organ/lesion segmentation further confirms that the derived transfer-aware mixtures provide stronger pretrained representations for clinical 3D medical imaging tasks.
